vowels.title: Basic vowels
vowels.concept: Hangul is the Korean alphabet. Each syllable is a block. A vowel alone is written with **ㅇ** in front, which is silent at the start: 아 is just “a”.

consonants.title: Basic consonants
consonants.concept: Put a consonant in front of a vowel to make a syllable block: **ㄱ + ㅏ = 가** (ga). Read the block from left to right.

words.title: First words
words.concept: Join syllable blocks to make words. Read each block, then say them together.

greetings.title: Hello and thank you
greetings.concept: Polite greetings end in **-요** or **-니다**. 안녕하세요 works any time of day.

answers.title: Yes, no and okay
answers.concept: Short polite answers you can use every day. Korean adds **요** at the end to be polite.

meeting.title: Nice to meet you
meeting.concept: When you meet someone new, say 만나서 반갑습니다. There are two ways to say goodbye: one for the person leaving, one for the person staying.

self.title: I am a student
self.concept: **저는** means “I” (polite). Put **이에요** after a consonant and **예요** after a vowel to say “I am …”.

family.title: My family
family.concept: Family words are used a lot in Korean, even for people who are not family.

numbers.title: Counting
numbers.concept: Korean has two number systems: native Korean (하나, 둘, 셋 …) for counting things, and Sino-Korean (일, 이, 삼 …) for money, dates and minutes.

verbs.title: Everyday verbs
verbs.concept: Polite present-tense verbs end in **-아요 / -어요 / -해요**. The same form is used for “I”, “you” and “they”.

places.title: Going to places
places.concept: Put **에** after a place to say where you go or come: 학교에 가요. The verb comes last.

objects.title: Eating, drinking, reading
objects.concept: The object of a verb gets **을** after a consonant and **를** after a vowel: 밥을 먹어요, 커피를 마셔요.

time.title: Yesterday, today, tomorrow
time.concept: Time words usually come near the start of the sentence.

past.title: What I did
past.concept: Past tense: **-았어요 / -었어요 / -했어요**. Some verbs shorten: 가다 → 갔어요, 보다 → 봤어요.

plans.title: What I will do
plans.concept: Use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요** for plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.

shopping.title: At the shop
shopping.concept: Ask the price with 얼마예요? and ask for something with **… 주세요** (… please).

directions.title: Where is it?
directions.concept: Ask **… 어디예요?** (Where is …?). Listen for 오른쪽 (right), 왼쪽 (left) and 직진 (straight).

wants.title: I want to …
wants.concept: Add **-고 싶어요** to a verb stem to say what you want to do: 가다 → 가고 싶어요.

gloss.willMeetFriend: I will meet a friend tomorrow.
gloss.willWatchMovie: I will watch a movie tomorrow.
gloss.wantGoKorea: I want to go to Korea.

note.gaseyo: 안녕히 가세요 is said to someone who is leaving; 안녕히 계세요 is said to someone who is staying.
note.ieyo: Use 이에요 after a consonant (학생 → 학생이에요) and 예요 after a vowel (의사 → 의사예요).
note.sino: This is a Sino-Korean number (일, 이, 삼 …), used for money, dates and minutes.
note.e: 에 marks the place you go to or come to.
note.verbEnd: Korean puts the verb at the end of the sentence.
note.eul: Use 을 after a consonant (밥을, 물을) and 를 after a vowel (커피를, 사과를).
note.past: Past tense: 가다 → 갔어요, 먹다 → 먹었어요, 보다 → 봤어요.
note.future: -(으)ㄹ 거예요 talks about plans: 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
note.won: 천 = 1000, so 오천 = 5000. 원 is the Korean currency (won).
note.want: -고 싶어요 means “want to”: 가다 → 가고 싶어요, 먹다 → 먹고 싶어요.
